passage: Keyboard instruments in the early Baroque period were often tuned in a system called meantone temperament, which makes the most common keys sound especially pure but leaves a few remote keys badly out of tune—so harsh that musicians nicknamed one interval the "wolf." A composer writing for such an instrument therefore had a strong practical reason to keep to the keys the tuning favored. From this it follows that a Baroque keyboard piece that freely modulates into many remote keys ______
question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: was most likely intended for an instrument tuned in some system other than strict meantone temperament.
could have been performed in tune on any meantone-tuned keyboard instrument.
must have been composed before meantone temperament came into common use.
would have sounded especially pure precisely in those remote keys when played on a meantone-tuned instrument.

explanation: The correct answer is A. The premises are that meantone tuning makes remote keys harsh and that composers writing for meantone instruments had reason to avoid those keys. A piece that ranges freely into many remote keys would sound badly out of tune on a meantone instrument, so it was most likely written for a different tuning. Choice B contradicts the premise that remote keys sound harsh in meantone. Choice C makes an unsupported claim about the date. Choice D reverses the premise by claiming the remote keys would sound especially pure.

_meta.anchor: Meantone temperament; remote keys sound harsh, implying a different tuning
